headline_marked: Banned [[Chhatra League holds procession]] in Dhaka's Mohakhali
headline: Banned Chhatra League holds procession in Dhaka's Mohakhali
summary: Hundreds of activists marched to mark the Awami League's anniversary and demand the release of political prisoners, leading to police detentions.
details: Several hundred activists of the banned Chhatra League, the student wing of the Awami League, held a procession in Dhaka's Mohakhali on Thursday morning.
The march began around 9am from the Mohakhali Bus Stand, with demonstrators carrying banners and shouting slogans.
Participants called for the release of 'political prisoners' and celebrated the Awami League's founding anniversary.
The procession was joined by approximately 20 to 25 women from the Jubo Mohila League along the way.
Slogans included 'Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu' and calls for the return of Sheikh Hasina.
Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station chief Md Mahbubur Rahman confirmed that some people took to the streets and two individuals have been detained.
Police are currently working to track down other participants of the banned gathering.
caption:
Hundreds of activists from the banned Chhatra League took to the streets of Mohakhali today.

Several hundred activists of the banned Chhatra League, the student wing of the Awami League, held a procession in Dhaka's Mohakhali on Thursday morning.

The march began around 9am from the Mohakhali Bus Stand, with demonstrators carrying banners and shouting slogans.

Participants called for the release of 'political prisoners' and celebrated the Awami League's founding anniversary.

The procession was joined by approximately 20 to 25 women from the Jubo Mohila League along the way.

Slogans included 'Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu' and calls for the return of Sheikh Hasina.

Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station chief Md Mahbubur Rahman confirmed that some people took to the streets and two individuals have been detained.

Police are currently working to track down other participants of the banned gathering.

headline_marked: Death toll rises to 4 as [[another body recovered from Meghna River]] in Narsingdi
headline: Death toll rises to 4 as another body recovered from Meghna River in Narsingdi
summary: The body of Abdul Latif, 35, was found floating in the river, believed to be a victim of recent turf wars between rival groups in Raipura Upazila.
details: Police recovered the body of 35-year-old Abdul Latif from the Meghna River in the Gopinathpur area of Nilakshya Union on Thursday afternoon.
Local sources state that the death toll from recent violence between rival groups fighting over turf in Narsingdi's Raipura Upazila has now risen to four.
The deceased was found wearing a police vest. Raipura Police Station chief Md Mujibur Rahman confirmed the recovery and stated the body has been sent for post-mortem.
Previous victims include Bulbul Mia (35) and Anik Mia (22), whose bodies were found Tuesday, and Kawsar Mia (35), who was found Wednesday with spear wounds.
The violence reportedly stems from a power struggle involving supporters of local leader Joba Member and an opposing group.
The conflict escalated after a migrant worker named Mamun was shot dead on December 8, 2025, leading several suspects to go into hiding.
caption:
Four people are now dead after a series of violent turf clashes in Narsingdi, with the latest body recovered from the Meghna River.

Police recovered the body of 35-year-old Abdul Latif from the Meghna River in the Gopinathpur area of Nilakshya Union on Thursday afternoon.

Local sources state that the death toll from recent violence between rival groups fighting over turf in Narsingdi's Raipura Upazila has now risen to four.

The deceased was found wearing a police vest. Raipura Police Station chief Md Mujibur Rahman confirmed the recovery and stated the body has been sent for post-mortem.

Previous victims include Bulbul Mia (35) and Anik Mia (22), whose bodies were found Tuesday, and Kawsar Mia (35), who was found Wednesday with spear wounds.

The violence reportedly stems from a power struggle involving supporters of local leader Joba Member and an opposing group.

The conflict escalated after a migrant worker named Mamun was shot dead on December 8, 2025, leading several suspects to go into hiding.
